skip_reason: Not a sales call - inbound customer service and claims call on an already-completed move. Faye Cox was moved Thursday 8/27 out of the Dallas branch and called about four post-move issues: an hourly rate she believed she was not quoted for the Sunday cleanup trip (resolved in-call when she found the $101-per-mover line on her own quote), a $115 travel fee she wanted waived because only one truck was sent Thursday, a missing power cord for an adjustable bed, and a damaged Traeger grill cover needing a damage claim. No quote, no pricing pitch for new business, no booking attempt - nothing the 85-point sales scorecard measures. Jack is also the Garland branch manager handling another branch's customer, not a sales rep working a lead.
top_strength: Not scored (skip). Factually: strong service recovery - Jack found the profile across branches under a different name, waived the $115 travel fee on the spot with a clear reason, arranged for the on-site crew to locate the bed cord that day, sent a damage claim link by text, and committed to briefing the Dallas manager himself. Closed by recapping all four action items and asking "Does that sound about right?"
coaching_note: Not scored (skip). Worth flagging outside the grading roster: the root cause was a sales/dispatch failure, not a service failure - the customer described a home plus two storage units and was sent one truck, forcing a second trip, a second travel fee and a Sunday rate she had not internalized. That is an estimate-accuracy and scoping miss on the original booking, and the customer's own movers said on site "they should have sent us with two trucks." Also note two damage items from one move (grill cover, garage shelving) with the shelving already discarded and unclaimed.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently de-escalating with an initially incensed customer - "No you're good. No you're good," "Right, of course," took ownership across branch lines, and she ended with "I appreciate you handling it even though you're in Garland."
